# Utf8Error

What was wrong with a byte sequence.

```rux
pub enum Utf8Error: int32 {
    Truncated = 1,
    InvalidStart = 2,
    InvalidContinuation = 3
}
```

The cases are distinguished because they mean different things about where the bytes came from. `Truncated` is
what a buffer boundary looks like and may just mean read more; the rest mean the bytes are not UTF-8 and no
amount of reading will change that. Every case is a failure: the functions here report success through the other
channel of the native fallible they return.

## Cases

| Name                  | Value | Description                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| --------------------- | ----- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Truncated`           | `1`   | A sequence starts but the bytes run out before it ends.                                                                                                                                                  |
| `InvalidStart`        | `2`   | A byte that cannot start a sequence: a continuation byte on its own, or one of the values UTF-8 never uses.                                                                                              |
| `InvalidContinuation` | `3`   | A byte where a continuation byte was required, or a continuation outside the range this leading byte allows — which is what rejects an overlong form, a surrogate half, or a value past the last scalar. |
